questions.q: What does Altucher suggest looking for as a starting passion?
a: Something you loved doing as a child
The highest-paying skill you can learn
A field with the most job openings
Whatever your parents recommend
questions.why: Lesson 1 says childhood interests, even impractical ones, provide a starting point.

questions.q: What can daily practice do with your pain, according to the summary?
a: Turn it into work that helps you and others
Remove it completely over time
Hide it from the people around you
Make success harder to notice
questions.why: Lesson 2 says channeling pain into your passion lets it help both you and other people.

questions.q: How did Eminem's difficult upbringing serve his career?
a: It became the raw material for his songs
It gave him access to better schools
It taught him to avoid public attention
It shielded him from criticism
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes poverty and bullying becoming fuel for the music that built his career.

questions.q: What question does Altucher suggest for checking a decision?
a: Did I choose this out of fear or for growth?
Will this choice make me look successful?
Would my family approve of this step?
Is this the safest option available?
questions.why: Lesson 3 says aligning choices with your values starts with spotting fear-based decisions.

questions.q: Why do family businesses often fail after a few generations, according to Altucher?
a: Each generation's values drift from the original
They refuse to hire anyone outside the family
They expand faster than demand allows
They neglect to advertise their products
questions.why: Lesson 3 blames a mismatch of values between founders and the successors who inherit the firm.
